root_cause.text: The io_uring NAPI busy poll implementation did not enforce an upper bound on the `busy_poll_to` time, allowing an unlimited polling duration without rescheduling, which could cause the task to appear stuck and trigger kernel preemption complaints.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "no cap on the maximum amount of time that napi is allowed to poll if no events are found", and the patch caps `busy_poll_to` to 10 msec via `napi->busy_poll_to = min(10000, napi->busy_poll_to);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against overly large busy poll timeout values by capping NAPI polling time to 10 ms.
intent_record.what: Added a line that caps `napi->busy_poll_to` to a maximum of 10000 microseconds (10 ms) using `min()`.
intent_record.how: After setting `napi_track_mode`, the function now clamps the user-provided busy poll timeout to at most 10 ms before converting it to nanoseconds and storing it in the ring context, preventing excessively long spin times.

grouping_result.intent: Guard against overly large busy poll timeout values by capping NAPI polling time to 10 ms.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by capping the busy poll timeout to prevent unlimited polling duration.

candidates.rationale: This statement writes the user-provided busy poll timeout value without any upper bound check, allowing an arbitrarily large timeout that can cause the task to spin without rescheduling, leading to preemption complaints.
